title: End-to-End Loan Analysis Dashboard
summary: A Power BI project for exploring loan distribution, applicant demographics and financial risk patterns.
problem: Understanding loan distribution, applicant profiles and financial risk across multiple dashboard views.
whyItMatters: Bringing these views together can make patterns in loan data easier to explore. This is a learning project, not evidence of lending outcomes.
whatIBuilt: A practice Power BI dashboard with loan overview, applicant demographics, and financial risk views; documented transformations, YoY/YTD measures, validation, and interactive visuals.
categoryNote: Editorial classification from supplied title; methods not confirmed.

blocks.text: The README frames the analysis around customer behavior, loan distribution and financial risk patterns.
Excel / CSV is listed as an input format. Dataset origin, collection period, licensing and sample size have not been supplied.
Power Query transformations and data validation are documented. The exact transformation steps and validation records are not supplied.
Documented views explore loan purpose, employment, age groups, credit score categories, marital status, mortgage, dependents and education.

Power BI reports use DAX measures, YoY and YTD calculations, slicers, a decomposition tree and a Sankey visual. The owner-supplied resume separately lists SQL Server; its role is not detailed in the README.

The README lists default rate, year-over-year loan/default change and year-to-date analysis. These are dashboard measures, not predictive-model accuracy. Values and complete formulas are not supplied.
Three dashboard views are documented: Loan Overview, Applicant Demographics & Financial Profile, and Financial Risk Metrics. No numerical findings or independently reproduced outcomes are supplied.

title: Metron — Data Optimizer
summary: Compares ways to store analytical data for a stated workload, using measured local tests and data-integrity checks to explain a recommendation.
problem: Choosing among ways to store analytical data for a stated workload while preserving the data and making tradeoffs visible.
whyItMatters: Storage choices can affect query behavior and cost. The local MVP is designed to explain tested options and unknowns; modeled savings are not customer savings.
whatIBuilt: A local MVP comparing analytical data representations with integrity checks, bounded Docker benchmarks, cost assumptions, recommendations, asynchronous jobs, a dashboard, and portable reports.
categoryNote: Editorial browse category based on README scope.

blocks.text: Compare analytical dataset representations for a stated workload and recommend a tested feasible option with supporting evidence and explicit unknowns.

The current README supports CSV, NDJSON and Parquet input. No owner dataset provenance is supplied. The resume describes an earlier advisor with a 1,000-row synthetic demo; that is a separate version, not a current real-world dataset claim.
The README describes file validation, local metadata profiling and lossless conversion. Exact typed integrity checks preserve duplicate counts and distinguish feasibility from performance.
Candidate enumeration, workload-guided layouts and ranking are documented. This is an optimization and comparison workflow; no trained predictive model or accuracy claim is established.

The current local MVP documents Docker-isolated benchmarks, asynchronous assessment jobs, a dashboard and portable reports. Current README tools and the earlier resume Streamlit/YAML stack remain separately attributed.

The README distinguishes integrity checks, measured local load/query timings, physical bytes and modeled costs. Synthetic or user-supplied price assumptions must stay labeled. These tests do not establish cloud latency or concurrency.
The README reports a local MVP. Portfolio review did not execute its code, reproduce timings or verify production/customer outcomes. No speedup or savings figure is claimed here.

title: CredResolve — Collections Intelligence Dashboard
summary: Brings collection performance, data-quality issues, recovery funnels and channel comparisons into one dashboard.
problem: Understanding collections performance while identifying data-quality issues that could distort reported recovery.
whyItMatters: Teams need clear metric definitions and reliable records to compare channels and investigate recovery. The dashboard presents scenarios, not proven business gains.
whatIBuilt: A dashboard exploring recovery performance, data-quality issues, recovery funnels, channel comparisons, and investment scenarios. Filters and validated dataset/API connections are future work in the README.
categoryNote: Editorial browse category based on README scope.

blocks.text: Bring recovery performance, data reliability, channel comparisons and investment scenarios into one dashboard for investigation.
Dataset provenance and data lineage are not supplied. Connecting a validated analytics dataset or backend API is listed as future work.

The README proposes checking missing/inconsistent records, duplicate payments, timezone issues and attribution conflicts. This is a described analytical approach; executed cleaning steps are not established.

The dashboard documents a recovery funnel: Targeted → Contacted → Right Party Contact → Promise to Pay → PTP Kept → Paid. Channel comparisons are described; no verified conversion or performance values are supplied.

The README explicitly lists HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the web dashboard. Python and SQL come separately from the owner-supplied resume. Reporting-period, channel and segment filters are future improvements, not working features claimed here.

Recovery rate, promise-to-pay kept rate, recovery per agent-hour, cost per rupee recovered and ROI scenarios are described. Exact formulas and denominators need documentation; scenario expectations are not observed gains.
The README describes dashboard views and screenshot references. No reproduced recovery increase, ROI improvement, client deployment or public demo has been supplied.
README proposals include period/channel/segment filters, a validated dataset/API connection, KPI formulas and lineage, automated quality checks, controlled experiments and exportable reports.
